newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Analysts' reactions to Skandia, Stadshypotek mixed.
newsitem.headline: Analysts' reactions to Skandia, Stadshypotek mixed.

text.p: Analysts' reactions to news of a proposed merger between Swedish insurer Skandia and mortgage bank Stadshypotek announced on Monday morning were mixed.
The merger will create the Nordic region's leading finance company with total assets of about 500 billion crowns ($75.3 billion).
"It came as a total surprise," said one London-based insurance analyst who asked not to be named.
"Our banking analysts had expected Stadshypotek was a takeover target as the stock price has shot up in the past few weeks but Skandia came as a shock.

"Skandia has a relatively good home market operation and some rapidly growing markets overseas. Why is it doing this? It is diluting the attractiveness of Skandia by merging with a large mortgage bank at home which is not well-placed in competitiveness."
BZW analyst Angus Runciman said the news was not entirely unexpected.
"There had been rumours around the market late last week, so it has not come as a complete surprise," he said.
Runciman said Skandia was looking for a domestic partner and needed a boost to help cover its debts.

"It looks as though Skandia would benefit more from the merger. Their major rationale is to pay down Skandia's debts...It looks as though they are trying to find a domestic partner to help finance AFS (Skandia's Assurance and Financial Services)."
Over the weekend the Swedish government announced it was selling the state's 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek to an industrial buyer through a controlled auction.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Thursday in a parliamentary budget debate that the government would seek the highest possible price for Stadshypotek.
Runciman said a higher bid for the government's 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek was possible following the proposed merger.
Both companies said the government had not been willing to discuss the proposed merger.
"Our feeling is that the government has clearly left the way open for a higher bid for Stadshypotek, which means there is room for some further upside in Stadshypotek," Runciman said.
"We think this one is not over. This is not a done deal yet, considering the way it has been left open by the government."
